articles.title: India may face 2-million-tonne sugar gap; imports could be key: Dalmia Bharat Sugar’s Kapil Nema
articles.description: India could face a sugar shortfall of around 2 million tonne, making the timing of any imports a key policy decision for the government, according to Kapil Nema, Deputy Executive Director-Sugar & Ethanol Business at Dalmia Bharat Sugar & Industries.Nema expects Indian sugar inventories to settle at around 5–5.5 million tonne, while current stocks stood at 36 lakh tonne as of October 1. With the government keeping a close watch on inventories and the supply pipeline remaining tight, he sees a gap of around 2 million tonne that may eventually need to be filled through imports.“There is a gap of around 2 million tonne which needs to be filled,” Nema said. He added that the government will need to decide when to allow imports, with two possible windows—after the current crushing season ends or just before the next season begins.The domestic supply outlook has also become less comfortable because of weather conditions. Nema said recent rains in Uttar Pradesh have raised concerns about the cane crop and could reduce sugar output from the state by around 100,000–200,000 tonne. Maharashtra and Karnataka have also seen weak rainfall, particularly in August, although some rains arrived in September.Globally, sugar prices have turned bullish on expectations of lower Brazilian production. Rains have slowed crushing in Brazil, while more carryover cane than initially expected could push Brazilian sugar production estimates lower. Nema said estimates are now around 37.5–38.5 million tonne, compared with earlier expectations of higher output.“Overall market is reading it as bullish, and that's why we saw the rally on Friday,” Nema said, referring to the sharp rise in international sugar prices.However, he does not see a major global supply deficit when raw and white sugar are considered together. Instead, the market has a surplus of around 2–2.5 million tonne in raw sugar, while white sugar has a deficit of about 1 million tonne. The key question is whether the raw sugar surplus can be converted into white sugar through refining, which would require adequate incentives for refiners.Watch the full conversation hereOn ethanol, Nema expects no sugar diversion in the first tender cycle until there is greater clarity on the size of the Indian crop. However, if the crop eventually turns out to be comfortable, the government could allow some B-heavy molasses to be diverted to ethanol in subsequent tender cycles.“I believe unlike last year where there was only one ethanol tender, there's going to be multiple cycles this time,” Nema said. He does not expect syrup diversion at this stage.Catch all the latest updates from the stock market here

articles.title: Fire tender called to clean Gujarat BJP MLA's bungalow, triggers debate over alleged misuse
articles.description: Gujarat BJP MLA Bachubhai Khabad has found himself in hot water after videos showed a fire department vehicle from the Devgadh Baria Municipality cleaning the politician's bungalow. The videos showed water being sprayed at Khabad’s residence in Dhanpur taluka. The incident has triggered debate over alleged misuse after videos went viral on social media platforms.
